classification.summary: MokeRelease.settle() allowed any EOA to overwrite settledMokePrice with the instantaneous MOKE/WBNB and WBNB/USDT AMM spot price. The attacker distorted the WBNB/USDT reserve ratio, settled the manipulated price, and then claimed 43.86 million MOKE against genuine stored release quotas; claim()'s deviation check compared the live price to the just-manipulated settled price and therefore did not protect the reserve.

loss.notes: The MOKE/WBNB PancakeSwap pair 0xba6a49a97cc725b3c39d6c5ea6deffddb64fe6b8 paid 1664.616180024096154954 WBNB in the exploit's MOKE sale: its Swap event at log 209 records 43860308.980417278429035188 MOKE in and exactly that WBNB amount out. This is the defect-caused gross loss to liquidity providers. The pair's end-of-block WBNB reserve fell by the larger 1692.745266365074783560 WBNB, from 1849.174363661815743493 at block 113652608 to 156.429097296740959933 at block 113652609, but the other 28.129086340978628606 WBNB was paid in the separate Burn event at log 108 against LP tokens the attacker already owned, so it was a withdrawal of pre-positioned liquidity rather than loss caused by the defect. DefiLlama prices BNB at 588.2809941793458 USD seven seconds before the incident. The legacy USD 907,700 estimate tracks the attacker's lower post-financing proceeds rather than the pair's gross loss.

lastCodeChange.description: Direct MokeRelease creation by 0xf5aa24b07be11b53498bd4cf311e68f15ac3653e. Its runtime hash is 0x4abe91cc475b04c64bac7b7d7b783bfc6388884db171cc41aa86665ce2916f9d both in the deployment block and immediately before the exploit, and its EIP-1967 implementation and beacon slots are zero. The verified contract is not a proxy, so deployment is the only executable-code change.

sources.note: Anchor kept. The attacker EOA 0xe454a9bac1a44868e4a9cbe1a4b5ac231d0dcf8a installed an EIP-7702 delegation to attacker implementation 0xc7fdea027feb41c8f3a45ec284280ce68f4e6ff7 in type-4 transaction 0xc0f1df63 at block 113652442: cast recover-authority recovers the same EOA from the authorization, and its code immediately before the exploit is 0xef0100c7fdea027feb41c8f3a45ec284280ce68f4e6ff7. The exploit itself is a type-2 self-call from and to that EOA, so the delegation is attacker packaging, not a victim upgrade or code-age anchor; the following type-4 transaction 0xb873f350 revokes it. No other surrounding attacker transaction calls MokeRelease. BscScan's verified MokeRelease source shows the actual defect: settle() admits any msg.sender == tx.origin and directly assigns getMokeUsdtPrice(), which multiplies instantaneous MOKE/WBNB and WBNB/USDT pair reserve ratios, to settledMokePrice. In the exploit trace the attacker distorts the WBNB/USDT reserve ratio, calls settle(), which emits PriceSettled(594140821297791), and then calls claim() from the EOA and three identical helper contracts. claim() is not entitlement-free: all four callers have stored totalQuotaUsdt and pendingUsdt, but its maxPriceDeviation check compares the live manipulated price to the just-manipulated settled price. The four claims release exactly 43860308.980417278429035188 MOKE from reserve pair 0x89715a0768e95942071ed52b37a90c6d53019b5a; the amount is routed through MokeLPDividend and sold into the MOKE/WBNB pair. The pair's Swap event records 43860308.980417278429035188 MOKE in and 1664.616180024096154954 WBNB out. Its additional 28.129086340978628606 WBNB outflow is separately identified by the preceding Burn event and redeems attacker-owned LP, so the raw reserve delta of 1692.745266365074783560 WBNB is not all defect-caused loss. Code history: MokeRelease is a direct top-level creation by 0xf5aa24b07be11b53498bd4cf311e68f15ac3653e in 0x2b2808c2 at block 111423896 index 112; runtime hash 0x4abe91cc475b04c64bac7b7d7b783bfc6388884db171cc41aa86665ce2916f9d matches at creation and immediately before the exploit, and both EIP-1967 code-selection slots are zero. The executed defect-bearing code is therefore 1003445 seconds old. DefiLlama's BNB observation is 588.2809941793458 USD at timestamp 1785703804, seven seconds before the exploit.
